## Libraries

```{r, echo = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(reticulate)
library(markovchain)
library(diagram)
library(gridExtra)
set.seed(12345)
```


## Full Transition Matrix as One Big Markov Chain

```{r}
tmA <- read.csv('~/Coding/Data/Farm_Model/trans_matrix.csv', header = TRUE)
tma <- tmA %>% as.matrix()
tmA
```
## Creating Markov Chains for each Climate

```{r}

stateNames = c('w1', 'w2', 'w3', 'w4', 'w5')

c1m <- tma[1:5,1:5]
c2m <- tma[6:10,6:10]
c3m <- tma[11:15,11:15]
c4m <- tma[16:20,16:20]

row.names(c1m) <- stateNames;colnames(c1m) <- stateNames
row.names(c2m) <- stateNames;colnames(c2m) <- stateNames
row.names(c3m) <- stateNames;colnames(c3m) <- stateNames
row.names(c4m) <- stateNames;colnames(c4m) <- stateNames

plotmat(c1m, 
        lwd = 1, box.lwd = 2, 
        cex.txt = 0.8, 
        box.size = 0.1, 
        box.type = "circle", 
        box.prop = 0.5,
        box.col = "light blue",
        arr.length=.1,
        arr.width=.1,
        self.cex = .6,
        self.shifty = -.01,
        self.shiftx = .1,
        main = "Climate 1 Markov Chain")

c1mc <- new("markovchain", transitionMatrix=c1m, states = c('w1', 'w2', 'w3', 'w4', 'w5'),
             name="climate1")

c2mc <- new("markovchain", transitionMatrix=c2m, states = c('w1', 'w2', 'w3', 'w4', 'w5'),
             name="climate2")

c3mc <- new("markovchain", transitionMatrix=c3m, states = c('w1', 'w2', 'w3', 'w4', 'w5'),
             name="climate3")

c4mc <- new("markovchain", transitionMatrix=c4m, states = c('w1', 'w2', 'w3', 'w4', 'w5'),
             name="climate4")


```

## Setting the Probabilities for Each Climate

```{r}

probc1 <- 0.60
probc2 <- 0.25
probc3 <- 0.10
probc4 <- 0.05


start <- runif(1)

if(start < probc1){climate <- 'c1'}
if(start >= probc1 & start < probc1+probc2){climate <- 'c2'}
if(start >= probc1+probc2 & start < probc1+probc2+probc3){climate <- 'c3'}
if(start >= probc1+probc2+probc3){ climate <- 'c4'}

print('Climate is equal to:')
climate



```


## Code for Markov Chain Sequence



```{r}
climate_realizations <- c()
precips <- c()
iters <- 1000
year_length <- 25

for(i in 1:iters){
  
start <- runif(1)

if(start < probc1){climate <- 'c1'}
if(start >= probc1 & start < probc1+probc2){climate <- 'c2'}
if(start >= probc1+probc2 & start < probc1+probc2+probc3){climate <- 'c3'}
if(start >= probc1+probc2+probc3){ climate <- 'c4'}

climate_realizations <- c(climate_realizations,climate)

if(climate == 'c1'){
  seq <- rmarkovchain(n = year_length,object = c1mc)
}

if(climate == 'c2'){
  seq <- rmarkovchain(n = year_length,object = c2mc)
}

if(climate == 'c3'){
  seq <- rmarkovchain(n = year_length,object = c3mc)
}

if(climate == 'c4'){
  seq <- rmarkovchain(n = year_length,object = c4mc)
}

precips <- c(precips,seq)

}
```

#Organizing and Summarizing Climate Realizations and Precipcatiation Information

```{r}
cm_in <- 2.54 # 2.54
rainfall_days_perc <- 0.70 # Use 75%

w1p <- 5 *cm_in * rainfall_days_perc
w2p <- 15 *cm_in * rainfall_days_perc
w3p <- 30 *cm_in * rainfall_days_perc
w4p <- 45 *cm_in * rainfall_days_perc
w5p <- 60 *cm_in * rainfall_days_perc

precips <- gsub('w1',as.character(w1p),precips)
precips <- gsub('w2',as.character(w2p),precips)
precips <- gsub('w3',as.character(w3p),precips)
precips <- gsub('w4',as.character(w4p),precips)
precips <- gsub('w5',as.character(w5p),precips)


climate_realizations <- as.factor(climate_realizations)
summary(climate_realizations)
precips <- as.numeric(precips)
summary(precips)

precips_df <- matrix(precips, ncol = year_length , byrow = T)
precips_df <- cbind(as.matrix(climate_realizations),precips_df)
precips_df <- precips_df %>% as_tibble() %>% arrange(V1)
precips <- precips_df %>% select(-V1) %>% t %>% as.vector %>% as.numeric




```

## Parameters and Conversions
```{python}
# Conversions

cm2_ha = 100000000 # 100,000,000 cm2 = 1 ha

cm3_gal = 3785.41 # 3785.41 cm2 = 1 Gal

m3_kGal = 3.785411784

gal_acre_ft = 325851 # 1 acre ft = 325851 gallons

acre_ha = 2.47105 # 1 hectare = 2.47105 acres

cm_ft = 30.48 # 1 ft = 30.48 cm

cm_in = 2.54

lb_tonne = 2204.62

# Hours in a Month
hrs_month = 720

#Days in Month
days_month = 30

#Growing Season Months
gs_months = 9

# Parameters

ha = 200 # hectares average size of texas farms 411 acres rounded up, https://www.texasagriculture.gov/About/TexasAgStats.aspx#:~:text=For%2036%25%20of%20producers%20in,by%2012%20acres%20from%202012.

price = 200 # $/ metric ton #https://www.indexmundi.com/commodities/?commodity=wheat

#note $ /acre ranges from $7-85 / acre assuming only a few cm of depth similiar price to irrigation water 


#Water production cost $0.40 / kGal convert to $ / cm
cost_alt_water = 0.40 / 1000 / cm3_gal * cm2_ha * ha


# 6.25 kWh / kGal > / Gal > / acre-ft > acre-cm > / ha-cm > kwh/cm
alt_water_elc = 6.25 / 1000 * gal_acre_ft / cm_ft * acre_ha * ha







# Irrigation Water Cost https://news.berkeley.edu/berkeley_blog/the-cost-of-irrigation-water-and-urban-farming/
#  Given in $ / cm from: $ 40 / acre-ft / gal_acre_ft / cm3_gal * cm2_ha * ha 

#cost_irrigation_water = 40 / gal_acre_ft / cm3_gal * cm2_ha * ha  # $ / cm 


# $7 / ac- in convert to $ / cm
cost_irrigation_water =  7 / cm_in * acre_ha * ha


# 1 kWh / kGal
irrigation_water_elc = 1 / 1000 * gal_acre_ft / cm_ft * acre_ha * ha


salt_conc = 2 # deciSiemens / meter = dS/m

salt_conc_water = 1 # deciSiemens / meter = dS/m

precip = 20 * cm_in # 20 inches of rain


 #  1.5 acre-ft / acre / yr halved for season https://www.nass.usda.gov/Publications/Highlights/2019/2017Census_Irrigation_and_WaterManagement.pdf
 
irrigation_water_limit = 0.5

max_irrigation_water = irrigation_water_limit * cm_ft 

# $ / kW of capacity
cost_alt_elc = 1500



cost_utility_elc = 0.08



#Renewable Energy

# Capacity Factor Solar https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2018/07/03/texas-getting-315-mw-of-solar-power/

cf_solar = 0.30

# Fu, R., Feldman, D., Margolis, R., 2018. U.S. Solar Photovoltaic System Cost Benchmark: Q1 2018. Tech. rep., National Renewable Energy Laboratory, Golden, CO.

solar_dollar_kW = 1500

# wInd Costs https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2019/08/f65/2018%20Wind%20Technologies%20Market%20Report%20FINAL.pdf

wind_dollar_kW = 840
```
## The Effect of Water on Profit and Crop Growth

```{python}

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

alt_water = 0
irrigation_water = 0
water = np.array(range(100))+20


# From Dinar et. al 1991 "Production functions relating crop yield, water quality and quantity, soil salinity and drainage volume"

y1 = (-3.350 + 0.2064*water - 0.0014*water*water + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water 
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc
               -0.071 * water * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water * salt_conc 
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc)

p1 = (y1*price*10 +
              -alt_water * (ha*cm2_ha/cm3_gal) * cost_alt_water +
              -irrigation_water * (ha*cm2_ha/cm3_gal) * cost_irrigation_water )

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

ax.plot(water,p1, label = 'Profit', color = 'red') # profit is red line
ax.set_title('Profit and Yield by Water Depth')
ax.set_xlabel('Water Depth (cm)')
ax.set_ylabel('Profit ($/10 ha)')
ax.set_ylim([-100,7200])
ax.grid(True)
ax.legend(loc = 'lower right')

ax2 = ax.twinx()
ax2.plot(water,y1*lb_tonne, label = 'Yield') # yield is blue line
ax2.set_ylabel('Yield (tonnes/ha)')
ax.set_ylim([-100,8500])
ax2.legend()
plt.show()




```

# Run with equal probablity of wet, dry, and moderate climates


```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp

m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(single_run, year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVars(single_run, obj = 1/len(single_run), name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstrs( (profit[r] == crop_yield.sum(r,'*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum(r,'*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum(r,'*') * cost_utility_elc
              for r in single_run)
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[r,y] <= alt_water_cap
               for r in single_run for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_single[r,y] + alt_water[r,y] + irrigation_water[r,y] >= water[r,y]
              for r in single_run for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_constr' )
             
# Making sure you can't throw away precipitation             
m.addConstrs( (rain_single[r,y] <= water[r,y]
              for r in single_run for y in year)
             ,name = 'precip_constr' )             
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[r,y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[r,y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[r,y]
               for r in single_run for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[r,y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for r in single_run for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[r,y] + utility_elc[r,y] >= elc[r,y]
               for r in single_run for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for r in single_run:
    for y in year :
            m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[r,y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[r,y]  - 0.0014*water[r,y]*water[r,y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[r,y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();



```

```{python}


import numpy as np

ycy = np.array(0)
yp = np.array(0)
yiw = np.array(0)
yaw = np.array(0)
yw = np.array(0)
yue = np.array(0)
yae = np.array(0)
ye = np.array(0)
yrain = np.array(0)

for i in year:
    ycy = np.append(ycy,np.mean([crop_yield[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    yp = np.append(yp,[profit[r].X for r in single_run])
    yiw = np.append(yiw,np.mean([irrigation_water[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    yaw = np.append(yaw,np.mean([alt_water[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    yw = np.append(yw,np.mean([water[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    yrain = np.append(yrain,np.mean([rain_single[r,i] for r in single_run]))
    yue = np.append(yue,np.mean([utility_elc[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    yae = np.append(yae,np.mean([alt_elc[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    ye = np.append(ye,np.mean([elc[r,i].X for r in single_run]))
    
ycy = ycy[1:(len(year)+1)]
yp = yp[1:(len(year)+1)]
yiw = yiw[1:(len(year)+1)]
yaw = yaw[1:(len(year)+1)]
yw = yw[1:(len(year)+1)]
yrain = yrain[1:(len(year)+1)]
yue = yue[1:(len(year)+1)]
yae = yae[1:(len(year)+1)]
ye = ye[1:(len(year)+1)]


ycy
yp
yiw
yaw
yw
yrain
yue
yae
ye
```

## Climate 1 Problem and Solution

```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp

m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in

alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVar(obj = 1, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstr( (profit == crop_yield.sum('*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum('*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum('*') * cost_utility_elc
              )
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[y] <= alt_water_cap
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c1_single[y] + alt_water[y] + irrigation_water[y] >= water[y]
              for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_constr' )


# Making sure you can't throw away precipitation             
m.addConstrs( (rain_c1_single[y] <= water[y]
              for y in year)
             ,name = 'precip_constr' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[y]
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[y] + utility_elc[y] >= elc[y]
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for y in year :
  m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[y]  - 0.0014*water[y]*water[y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )




m.update();



```

```{python}
m.optimize()
m.printQuality()
#print(m.display())

obj = m.getObjective()
alt_water_c1_single = alt_water_cap.X
alt_elc_c1_single = alt_elc_cap.X
print(obj.getValue())
alt_water_c1_single
alt_elc_c1_single
```

```{python, include = F}
alt_elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVar(obj = 1, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstr( (profit == crop_yield.sum('*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum('*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum('*') * cost_utility_elc
              )
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[y] <= alt_water_cap
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c4_single[y] + alt_water[y] + irrigation_water[y] >= water[y]
              for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_constr' )


# Making sure you can't throw away precipitation             
m.addConstrs( (rain_c4_single[y] <= water[y]
              for y in year)
             ,name = 'precip_constr' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[y]
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[y] + utility_elc[y] >= elc[y]
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for y in year :
  m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[y]  - 0.0014*water[y]*water[y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();



```

```{python, include = F}
for y in year :
  m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[y]  - 0.0014*water[y]*water[y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
```

## C0 realized in Climate 4 Problem and Solution

```{python, include = F}


import gurobipy as gp

m = gp.Model()

#m.params.NonConvex = 2 # Says its non convex but it is (FIXED quadratic constraints can't be equality)

# Set to maximize
m.ModelSense = -1

# Add variables

#First Stage Decision Variables Strategic Investment Decisions, pick what climate you are in which automatically picks how much alternative water to invest in


alt_water_cap = alt_water_c0_single
alt_elc_cap = alt_elc_c0_single

#alt_water_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_water_cap', lb = 0) # cm of depth
#alt_elc_cap = m.addVar(name = 'alt_elc_cap', lb = 0) # kW of depth


#Second Stage Decision Variables Operational Decisions, Pick how much water to use and how much irrigation water to buy

# Change these variables to be a function of option, climate, and season
water = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'water') # water used for crop, cm of depth
irrigation_water = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, ub = max_irrigation_water, name = 'irrigation_water') # cm of depth
alt_water = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_water') # alt_water used for crop, cm of depth
alt_elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'alt_elc') # alt_elc to power water, kWh
utility_elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'util_elc') # util_elc to power water, kWh
elc = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'elc') # total elc to power water, kWh

#Functions of the Above, also functions of option, climate, and season, 
crop_yield = m.addVars(year, lb = 0, name = 'yield') # tonne/ha
profit = m.addVar(obj = 1, name = 'profit') # $



#Maybe add a new profit variable that is the sum of the profit based on climate for easy coefficients



# Objective


m.addConstr( (profit == crop_yield.sum('*') * ha * price +
              -alt_water_cap * cost_alt_water  +
              -irrigation_water.sum('*') * cost_irrigation_water +
              -alt_elc_cap * cost_alt_elc +
              -utility_elc.sum('*') * cost_utility_elc
              )
            ,name = 'profit_constr')

# Water Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_water[y] <= alt_water_cap
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_cap' )
 

m.addConstrs( (rain_c4_single[y] + alt_water[y] + irrigation_water[y] >= water[y]
              for y in year)
             ,name = 'water_constr' )


# Making sure you can't throw away precipitation             
m.addConstrs( (rain_c4_single[y] <= water[y]
              for y in year)
             ,name = 'precip_constr' )
             
             
#Energy for Alt Water Equations    

m.addConstrs( alt_water[y] * alt_water_elc + irrigation_water[y] * irrigation_water_elc <= elc[y]
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_water' )

# Energy Capacity and Balance Equations

m.addConstrs( (alt_elc[y] <= alt_elc_cap * cf_solar * hrs_month * gs_months
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_cap' )




m.addConstrs( alt_elc[y] + utility_elc[y] >= elc[y]
               for y in year)
             ,name = 'elc_balance' )





for y in year :
  m.addQConstr( (crop_yield[y] <= -3.350 + 0.2064*water[y]  - 0.0014*water[y]*water[y]  + 
               3.555 * salt_conc_water + 2.326 * salt_conc_water*salt_conc_water +
               -2.031 * salt_conc + 0.823 * salt_conc*salt_conc +
               -0.071 * water[y]  * salt_conc_water + 0.033 * water[y]  * salt_conc +
               -2.754 * salt_conc_water * salt_conc
               )
               , name = 'crop_yield' )


m.update();



```

```{python}
m.optimize()
obj = m.getObjective()

print(obj.getValue())




```

```{r}
       alt_elc_cap_kW = c(py$alt_elc_c0_single, py$alt_elc_c1_single, py$alt_elc_c2_single, py$alt_elc_c3_single, py$alt_elc_c4_single),
       irrigation_cm = c(mean(py$yiw), mean(py$iwc1), mean(py$iwc2), mean(py$iwc3), mean(py$iwc4) ),
       alt_water_cm = c(mean(py$yaw), mean(py$awc1), mean(py$awc2), mean(py$awc3), mean(py$awc4) ),
       solar_prod_MWh = c(mean(py$yae),mean(py$aec1),mean(py$aec2),mean(py$aec3),mean(py$aec4)),
       util_elc_MWh = c(mean(py$yue),mean(py$uec1),mean(py$uec2),mean(py$uec3),mean(py$uec4)),
```

```{r}
stoch_df <- tibble(Year = seq(1,25), crop_yield = py$ycy, alt_water = py$yaw, alt_elc = py$yae, irrigation_water = py$yiw, utility_elc = py$yue, total_water = py$yw, total_elc = py$ye, precip = py$yrain, scenario = 'Stochastic_Model') %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, funs(round(.,2)))
```

```{r}
        plot.margin = unit(x = c(0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5), units = 'mm') ) +
  labs(title = 'MI-EP Moderate Climate Deterministic', y = 'Electricity Produced (MWh)', x = 'Year', size = 8) -> plot_c3_climate_elc

stochvclimate3_df %>%  
  pivot_longer(c(alt_elc,utility_elc,total_elc), names_to = 'ELC_Source', values_to = 'ELC_Depth') %>%
  filter(ELC_Source != 'total_elc') %>%
  filter(scenario == 'Moderate_Climate_Realized') %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = ELC_Depth/1000, group = ELC_Source, fill = ELC_Source, color = ELC_Source))+
  geom_area(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 1250, by = 250), limits =c(0,1250))+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 1, to = 25, by = 2))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = 'bold'), 
        legend.position = 'bottom', 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8), 
        legend.title = element_blank(), 
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust =0.5),
        legend.key.width = unit(0.06, 'in'), 
        legend.key.height = unit(0.06,'in'), 
        legend.margin = margin(t = 0, unit = 'cm'), 
        plot.margin = unit(x = c(0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5), units = 'mm') ) +
  labs(title = 'MI-EP Moderate Climate Realized', y = 'Electricity Produced (MWh)', x = 'Year', size = 8) -> plot_c3_climate_realized_elc
```
